D.t: John Hickenlooper leads by 21.0 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 593,561 votes; a one point swing is about 14,159 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +12.2 and D +29.3. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Denver, a projected net 224,458 votes; Boulder, a projected net 113,395 votes; Arapahoe, a projected net 102,326 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: El Paso, R +1.1, 11.9% of the vote; Douglas, R +0.7, 7.1% of the vote; Pueblo, D +8.1, 2.7% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, John Hickenlooper runs furthest behind in Weld, Larimer, Douglas. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 82% of voters, 56 to 41, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.08 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 73% of voters, 59 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.67 points; Incomes $50K to $124K, 55% of voters, 60 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.73 points.
The forecast's worst groups for John Hickenlooper: Immigration voters 22 to 75, Small counties 47 to 50, Midsize counties 50 to 47. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
